material_findings.title: EBL-Core provides an executable execution-boundary conformance profile for high-risk AI actions
material_findings.summary: arXiv:2609.11596, From Intent to Execution Grant, defines EBL-Core: a profile for deciding whether one canonical fully materialized AI-generated action candidate may receive action-scoped execution authority. It separates an Execution Release Contract from the actual Execution Grant and requires redemption-time validation, while binding intent, policy, evidence, context, time and a verifiable decision derivation.
material_findings.verification_evidence: The arXiv page exposes an ancillary reference artifact and a validation summary reporting 34/34 static vectors, 15/15 lifecycle checks, 100 concurrent-redemption trials with exactly one successful redemption/effect per trial, and 100 revoke-redeem races ending in valid terminal states. Those are author-provided retained-run results; this repository has not independently executed the artifact.
material_findings.scope_and_limits: The authors explicitly state that the bounded executable evidence does not establish human-intent correctness, evidence truth, complete mediation, production readiness, mechanized correctness or deployment-level security. This contribution therefore records EBL-Core only as a defensive architecture/evaluation lead and does not import code, alter authorization rules, or expand any target scope.
material_findings.recommended_action: When chronology reaches this Sep. 11 afternoon contribution, Build/Integration should download or otherwise preserve the complete arXiv ancillary artifact, verify its license/provenance, run the static/lifecycle/concurrency validation in an isolated benign environment, and compare EBL-Core's intent/policy/evidence/grant lifecycle against the suite's current authorization, provenance and recurring-agent contracts. Promote only specific controls that are reproducible and fit the existing canonical architecture.
